name: Coin Grow Core Curriculum
description: Ordered financial literacy progression from barter to investing. Each lesson builds on prior concepts. Age variants are generated from the same topic with different age_group inputs.

units.title: The Story of Money
units.theme: Where money comes from and why it exists

lessons.topic: What is money and why does it exist?
lessons.summary: Player experiences barter frustration (20 apples, get dinner). Discovers why a common medium of exchange was invented.

lessons.topic: Why save? The problem of things that rot.
lessons.summary: Player has 30 apples, must keep 10 for next week — but they rot. Discovers stores of value and the origin of saving.
Player witnesses the transition from commodity money (gold, grain) to symbolic money. Why does a coin have value? Because everyone agrees it does.

units.title: Earning and Spending
units.theme: Income, expenses, and the basics of a budget

lessons.summary: Player chooses between different ways to spend a day (trade skills, sell goods, work for someone). Discovers that income = exchanging value for money.

lessons.topic: Needs vs. wants: where does your money go?
lessons.summary: Player has a weekly income and must allocate it. Rent, food, and fun compete. Family happiness meter shows consequences of choices.

lessons.topic: What happens when you spend more than you earn?
lessons.summary: Player overspends and must borrow. Feels the weight of owing. Teases the concept of interest.

units.title: The Power of Saving
units.theme: Delayed gratification, goals, and compound growth

lessons.summary: Player picks a goal (bicycle, trip, new tool) and reverse-engineers how long it takes to save for it. Trophy awarded on completion.

lessons.topic: What is interest? Making your money work for you.
lessons.summary: Player discovers that a bank pays you to hold your money. Simulates leaving money in savings for 1, 5, and 20 years. Sees the curve.

lessons.topic: Compound interest: the eighth wonder of the world.
lessons.summary: Player races a friend who saves more but starts later. Demonstrates why starting early beats saving more.

units.title: Banks and Borrowing
units.theme: What banks do, credit, and responsible debt

lessons.topic: What does a bank actually do?
lessons.summary: Player runs a simple bank for a day — takes deposits, makes loans, charges interest. Sees how the system works from both sides.
Player takes two loans: one to buy a business tool (generates income), one to buy luxury goods (generates nothing). Compares outcomes.

units.title: Investing and Risk
units.theme: Making money grow, risk vs. reward, market basics

lessons.summary: Player allocates coins between three options: mattress (safe, 0% return), savings account (safe, low return), small business (risky, high return). Sees outcomes.

lessons.topic: Risk and return: why higher reward means higher risk.
lessons.summary: Player bets on harvests (weather risk), loans to merchants (default risk), and a new trade route (total loss risk). Discovers the risk-reward tradeoff.

lessons.topic: Diversification: don't put all eggs in one basket.
lessons.summary: Player with 3 merchant ships learns that spreading cargo across ships beats concentrating it. One ship sinks — outcome depends on player's split.
Player buys a tiny share of a village bakery. Bakery grows, struggles, recovers. Player decides when to hold, sell, or buy more.

units.title: Advanced Topics
units.theme: Inflation, taxes, insurance — the forces that affect your money

lessons.topic: What is inflation and why does it matter?
lessons.summary: Player saves coins under a mattress for 10 years. Returns to find everything costs more. Same coins, less buying power. Discovers inflation.
Player is the mayor for a day — must fund roads, schools, and a hospital. Decides who pays how much. Sees services disappear when taxes are cut.
Player's house burns down — with and without insurance. Then plays insurer for a village: collects small premiums, pays rare large claims. Sees the math.

market_simulator.description: Unlocked after completing Unit 5. Classroom-vs-classroom investment competition.
market_simulator.mechanics: Each classroom gets a virtual portfolio. Weekly market events generated by AI. Classes compete on returns over a semester.
